thread:
lina: Heads up — hitting a rough edge in the Python async client around error payloads. When server returns 422 with problem-details JSON, we end up with a generic ClientError and lose structured fields.
kevin: ugh. can you paste a minimal repro?
lina: yeah. here's what the server returns: ```json
{"type":"https://example.com/probs/validation","title":"Invalid input","status":422,"detail":"name: too short","errors":{"name":["min_length"]}}
```
lina: and the client code:```py
async with Client() as c:
    try:
        await c.create_user(payload)
    except ClientError as e:
        # e.status_code == 422 but no structured details on e.error_payload
        logger.info(e)
```
kevin: is e.raw_body present at least?
lina: sometimes. but it depends on where the exception is raised. auth middleware swallows/rewraps in a couple places. typing also only exposes str(e) and .status_code — no typed probe for problem details.
sam: that matches a bug I hit last month. we should preserve a .problem_details dict if content-type is application/problem+json or application/json with the expected keys.
anya: agree. also want each error class to be typed. e.g. ValidationError extends ClientError and has .errors: Dict[str, List[str]] so callers can pattern-match instead of parsing strings.
kevin: implementation proposal:
- preserve raw_body on exception object always (e.raw_body as bytes)
- if content-type indicates problem json, parse and attach e.problem_details (dict)
- add typed subclasses for 4xx like BadRequest, ValidationError, Unauthorized.
- keep backward-compatible fields: status_code, message, and __str__ unchanged
- avoid parsing for very large bodies (size cap)
- add unit tests for middleware order to make sure auth/retry layers don't drop the error payload
lina: sounds good. one extra: add e.retryable boolean that the client sets based on status + headers so higher-level code doesn't need to replicate logic.
kevin: careful — we currently have retry middleware deciding retryability later. But we can set a hint on the exception: e.should_retry = False/True. it's just a hint, not enforcement.
sam: also a doc snippet in exceptions.rst showing how to catch ValidationError and access .errors would be helpful for DX.
anya: typing note: expose these exception classes in top-level package so `from redwood import ValidationError` works with proper types for mypy.
kevin: agreed. plan: i'll open a PR with the exception hierarchy + attach problem_details + raw_body and unit tests. can someone file a GH issue with minimal repro?
lina: filing now. I'll include the server response and callback snippet.
ci-bot: Copied: Issue #4231 created by lina: "py-sdk: preserve problem-details on 4xx exceptions and add typed ValidationError"
kevin: thanks. timeline?
lina: PR should land early next week. I can help review the typing bits.
sam: we should also add an e.raw_text convenience property that decodes raw_body with best-effort charset detection.
kevin: good call. will include.
anya: small UX ask — make exception repr include status and short title, so quick logs show why it failed. e.g. "ValidationError(422: Invalid input)"
lina: perfect. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
kevin: assigning to myself and tagging @eng-ml for visibility since they rely on problem-details parsing in eval infra.
sam: ping me if you want help with tests across sync/async code paths. I hit the weird auth-wrap issue.
lina: done — thanks team.
